A certain officer of our army whilst engaged ina 
battle at Kiangwah, was attacked with a bayonet 

and as a result the intestines were exposed. He 
however did not stop and after placing the intestines 
Back into the body again started to fight against 4 or

"Kill t Kill : %. He is indeed a brave soldier. 


Although the enemy troops do not possess the same skill 
as we do but their uniform and other eyuipnments 

are much better than ours. When they are killed by us, 
their iron hats are seized and worn by our soldiers. 
The wearing of the iron hats ts a sign tyat we have 
killed an enemy soldier and so it is an honour. 

The majority of our soldiers at the front are at 
present wearing these hats. 


When Japanese cavadry rushed our line at Kiangwan our 
troops threw charcoal baskets upon them. These 

baskets formed obstacles to their advance and caused

Since fighting started many thousandaof Japanese ,

Japan. The latter have organized a gpwoup for demand-

when disarmed by our troops the Japanese soldiers 

bowed down and begged their liwes. This attitude is

Japanese women were unwilling to let their husbands leave

the moving of trains. The cruel militarists however

The train ran over and killed the women on the track.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
MUNICIPAL
File No. REGI ____
3360
S. 1, Special Branch
REPORT
Date February 1. 1935.

Subject Sale of pictorials of an Anti-Japanese nature

Made by ____ and Forwarded by D.I. Grubb

In accordance with the instructions of the
D.C. (Special Branch) regarding the suppression of the
sale of pictorials of an anti-Japanese nature by the
Tsung Shing Art Company, the Manager, Yu Chi-sen
(俞季), was interviewed, and strenuously denied
having recently stocked or sold any matter of an
inflammatory character. It is evident from his attitude
that he has learned of the seizures in Wayside District
and destroyed or otherwise disposed of his stock.
He was warned that the Municipal Police would take
immediate action against any printing house found issuing
matter likely to prove detrimental to the peace of the
Settlement.

H. Grubb.
D. I.

D.C. (Special Branch).
SI,
Please instruct staff and
agents to be on the look out for anti Japanese
literature which is being sold or otherwise
put into circulation and to report at once
any case that comes to their notice. The
papers may now be filed.

FEB. 2 1935

档案号 REGI ____
3360
S. 1，特务科
报告
日期：1935年2月1日。

主题：出售具有反日性质的画报

由 ____ 制作，经督察长 Grubb 转呈

遵照特务科副总监关于取缔宗圣艺术公司（Tsung Shing Art Company）出售具有反日性质画报的指示，该公司经理俞季森（Yu Chi-sen，音译：俞季）接受了问询，并极力否认近期进购或出售任何煽动性材料。从其态度来看，他显然已获悉在韦斯特区（Wayside District，即西区捕房辖区）发生的查扣行动，并已销毁或以其他方式处理了其库存。警方警告称，若发现任何印刷厂发行可能损害租界安宁的材料，工部局警务处将立即采取行动。

H. Grubb.
督察长。

致特务科副总监。
SI，
请指示职员及线员留意正在出售或以其他方式流通的反日文献，一旦发现此类情况，立即上报。
本案卷宗现可归档。

1935年2月2日

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. ____
S. B. REGISTER.
No. 33625
REPORT
Date January 31, 1935

Subject (in full) Sale of pictorials of an anti-Japanese nature.

Made by ____ and Forwarded by D. I. Grubb

Of the five pictorials of an anti-Japanese nature
forwarded from Wayside Station on January 30, 1935, four
of them bear the name and address of the publishers. They
are the Tsung Shing Art Co., 305/7 Canton Road. Inquiries
at this place reveal that these pictorials are being retailed
at $8.00 per 100.

According to a sales list issued by this Company,
four other kinds of anti-Japanese pictorials, bearing on
the hostilities locally and in the North-Eastern provinces,
are also being retailed.

The fifth pictorial gives as its origin the
Sing Ming (新民) Art Co., the location of which is unknown.

It is to be noted that these pictorials are not of
recent issue, being over two years old.

H. Grubb
D. I.

about the existence of these anti-Japanese
posters and the establishments responsible
for putting them into circulation with a view
to having the sale of them suppressed by indirect means.
This doubtful if a prosecution in the Court
would have the result.
JMcG 3 - 1935

档案号 ____
特务科登记簿。
编号 33625
报告
日期：1935年1月31日

主题（全称）：出售具有反日性质的画报。

由 ____ 制作，经督察长 D. I. Grubb 转呈

在1935年1月30日从韦斯特分局（Wayside Station）转来的五份具有反日性质的画报中，有四份印有出版商的名称和地址。它们是位于广东路305/7号的宗圣艺术公司（Tsung Shing Art Co.）。对该处的查询显示，这些画报的零售价为每百张8.00元。

根据该公司发布的销售清单，另有四种涉及本地及东北各省战事的反日画报也在零售。

第五份画报标明其来源为新民艺术公司（Sing Ming Art Co.），但其地点不详。

值得注意的是，这些画报并非近期出版，刊龄已超过两年。

H. Grubb
督察长。

（左侧手写批注）：
II.
BI，请
礼貌地劝告这些人
停止传播此类
宣传品。如果他们
不这样做，则将卷宗
转交 Jum 警司，按
指示采取行动。
JMcG

（下方手写批注）：
III.
Jum 警司

Wayside Station,
REPORT
Date January, 29, 19 35.
Subject Sale of Anti-Japanese pictures of the Sino-Japanese conflict.

Made by D.S.I. Hill. Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,
I beg to report, that at about 12 noon 29.1.35 Inspector Phillips attached to Wayside Station, handed to the under-signed a picture, the dimension of which measure 30½" X 21", which was exposed for sale by a Chinese picture hawker at Ward and Dalny Roads corner.

The picture shows imaginary and photographic scenes of the Sino-Japanese Shanghai "Incident" of 1932.

On the reverse side of the picture, is a brief outline of the Japanese Policy towards Chinese dating since 1874 the Japanese occupation of Formosa.

The undersigned communicated with Mr. Robertson A.C.P. Special Branch and explained that the picture was similar to the Anti-Japanese pictures recently distributed through the sale of "Chiu Wang" cigarettes.

In order to locate the hawker previously referred to the undersigned accompanied by Inspector Phillips proceeded to Ward and Dalny Roads corner, but no trace of the former could be found.

At 5 p.m. Inspector Phillips accompanied by J.D.S. 4. Watanabe, brought to the station four pictures, similar to that previously reported, showing scenes of the Sino-Japanese conflict, which they obtained from a street hawker on East Seward Road.

The pictures in question are forwarded herewith to Officer i/c Special Branch for information.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
[Signature]
Senior Det 1/c.

先生，
谨此报告，1935年1月29日中午12时许，隶属韦斯特分局的 Phillips 巡官向卑职递交了一张尺寸为30½英寸 X 21英寸的图片，该图片由一名中国图片小贩在沃德路（Ward Road，今长治路）与达尔尼路（Dalny Road，今丹徒路）拐角处公开出售。

该图片展示了1932年上海中日“事变”的想象场景和摄影照片。

敬礼，

高级侦探长。

September 14, 33.

"January 28" and "May 9" Humiliation Pictorials.

D.S.I. Golder

The attached file containing copies of
"January 28" and "May 9" Humiliation Pictorials was
shown to Mr. K.S. Kum, Assistant Municipal Advocate,
on September 14 and his opinion sought as to their
suppression. He contended that the books did not
warrant prosecution on the grounds of their contents but
as they have not been registered with the Chinese
Authorities as laid down in the "New Publication Law
of 1930". Mr. Kum thought that a prosecution might be
based on the point. Later in conference with
Mr. R.T. Bryan, Municipal Advocate, Mr. Kum agreed
that prosecution would avail nothing.

D. S. I.

Officer i/c Special Branch.

pages.en:
Translation of Subtitles to
attached Chinese Pictorials

1. Japanese attempting to swim across Wentsaopang unnoticed.
2. Chinese heavy artillery damaging the Japanese Military
Headquarters at North Szechuen Road Extension.
3. Bombardment of Tien Tung An Station by Japanese.
4. Japanese forcing Chinese to carry Munitions of War
for them.
5. Execution of Kompo men who were employed as Snipers
by the Japanese.
6. A Chauffeur at Nantao forced to carry Ammunition in his
car by Japanese being patriotic run his car into the
Whangpoo River.
7. Japanese Aeroplanes brought down at Nanziang.
8. A Chinese named Wang Tsien Foh took two Japanese
disguised as Chinese to the front where he confessed that
he had been told by the Japanese to throw bombs at the
Chinese Soldiers. The Japanese were executed.
9. Chinese Soldiers placed their hats of trees to deceive
the Japanese who were defeated in a surprise attack by
the Chinese Soldiers.
10. General Tsai Ting Kai leading his men who fought so
bravely that they defeated the Japanese.
pages.zh:
所附中文图画的字幕翻译

1. 日本人试图 unnoticed（不被察觉地）游过蕴藻浜（Wentsaopang）。
2. 中国重炮损坏了北四川路延伸段（North Szechuen Road Extension）的日本军事总部。
3. 日本人轰炸天通庵站（Tien Tung An Station）。
4. 日本人强迫中国人为其运送军火。
5. 处决被日本人雇佣为狙击手的高邮人（Kompo men）。
6. 南市（Nantao）的一名司机因爱国情怀，在被日本人强迫用车运送弹药时，将车开进了黄浦江。
7. 日本飞机在南翔（Nanziang）被击落。
8. 一名叫王钱佛（Wang Tsien Foh，音译）的中国人将两名伪装成中国人的日本人带到前线，他承认是日本人让他向中国士兵投掷炸弹。这两名日本人被处决。
9. 中国士兵将帽子挂在树上以迷惑日本人，中国士兵发动突袭击败了日本人。
10. 蔡廷锴将军率领部下英勇作战，击败了日本人。

pages.en:
Translation of Subtitles to
attached Chinese Pictorials

1.  A Chinese country woman bewailing the loss of her
    husband and family alleged to have been killed by
    Japanese.

2.  The arrest of Chinese secretly transporting munitions
    of War in coffins for the Japanese.

3.  The arrest of Chinese (Kompo men) who were paid $30/
    per day for carrying Land Mines for the Japanese.

4.  A Chinese woman at Shiozanchen was raped by three
    Japanese who afterwards stabbed her to death.

5.  Twenty or thirty sampans plied near the O.S.K. Japanese
    Wharf by Kompo men engaged in smuggling Motors for
    Military purposes.

6.  Japanese Plain Clothes Men letting loose Bloodhounds ?
    to eat the corpses of Chinese killed in battle.

7.  During hostilities near Kiangwan Chinese used big guns
    of new pattern to annihilate the Japanese Soldiers.

8.  General Tsai Ting Kai visiting wounded Chinese Soldiers.

9.  Aeroplane battle between Chinese and Japanese at Hangchow.

10. After serious fighting at Miaohanchen a Japanese General
    plunged into the river to escape but was captured by the
    Chinese Soldiers.
pages.zh:
所附中文图画的字幕翻译

1. 一名中国农村妇女哀悼据称被日本人杀害的丈夫和家人。

2. 逮捕秘密用棺材为日本人运输军火的中国人。

3. 逮捕受雇每天收取30美元为日本人搬运地雷的中国人（高邮人）。

4. 肖家镇（Shiozanchen，音译）的一名中国妇女被三名日本人强奸，随后被刺死。

5. 二十或三十艘舢板在大阪商船会社（O.S.K.）日本码头附近由高邮人驾驶，从事走私军用马达的活动。

6. 日本便衣人员放出猎犬？啃食在战斗中丧生的中国人的尸体。

7. 在江湾（Kiangwan）附近的敌对行动中，中国人使用新型大炮歼灭日本士兵。

8. 蔡廷锴将军探望受伤的中国士兵。

9. 中日在杭州进行的空战。

10. 在庙行镇（Miaohanchen，音译）经过激烈战斗后，一名日本将军跳河逃跑，但被中国士兵俘虏。

The following is the statement of Yen Jen-yuan (嚴仁元)
native of Zangzoh taken by me D.S. Golder
at Central Stn. on the March 10, 1932, and interpreted by Clerk Kao Yen-keng.

My name is Yen Jen-yuan (嚴仁元), aged 38,
married, native of Zangzoh, a hawker and living at 11
Chien Yue Li, Nan Yang Jao, off Boulevard de Montigny.
On learning the profit in selling newspapers, I proceeded
at 10.15 a.m. March 10, to Shantung Road near Foochow Road,
where I bought from a newspaper wholesale dealer 30 copies
of the pictorial seized by the Police at 2 coppers each.
These papers I could sell again at 4 coppers each copy.
At 10.20 a.m. ~~and~~ at the corner of Hankow and Honan
Roads, I was taken into custody by a foreign policeman.
I have no knowledge of the printing place and
the publisher of the lit/erature. I am not a communist
nor have I any connection with any anti-Japanese societies.

the sale of crackers for the present. Officers in charge of
Police stations should be directed to warn shops selling
crackers in the Settlement that they should refrain from
selling at present and daily enquiries should be made to
see that they are not doing so.

3. Assaults on Japanese. Such assaults in the streets of the
Settlement are a menace to the peace and good order of the
Settlement and are likely to have serious repercussions.
Such assaults, if they occur in an area that is well policed
are a reflexion on the high reputation of the Police. Every
effort should be made to prevent such assaults and if they
occur, to apprehend the persons guilty. All ranks should be
impressed with the need for the greatest vigilance in this
matter.

(Sd) F.W. Gerrard.
Commissioner of Police

pages.en:
WAR PICTORIAL No.2.

1. A certain officer of our army whilst engaged in a battle at Kiangwan, was attacked with a bayonet and as a result the intestines were exposed. He however did not stop and after placing the intestines back into the body again started to fight against 4 or 5 enemy soldiers. He was forcibly removed by rescuers to a hospital. On the way he continuously shouted : "Kill ! Kill ! ". He is indeed a brave soldier.

2. Although the enemy troops do not possess the same skill as we do but their uniform and other equipments are much better than ours. When they are killed by us, their iron hats are seized and worn by our soldiers. The wearing of the iron hats as a sign that we have killed an enemy soldier and so it is an honour. The majority of our soldiers at the front are at present wearing these hats.

3. When Japanese cavalry rushed our line at Kiangwan our troops threw charcoal baskets upon them. These baskets formed obstacles to their advance and caused disorder among the enemy troops. Seizing this opportunity our troops rushed them and gained a big victory.

4. Since fighting started many thousands of Japanese soldiers were killed leaving their wives behind in Japan. The latter have organized a group for demanding the return of their husbands from the Government. A Similar movements have started in Shanghai.

5. When disarmed by our troops the Japanese soldiers bowed down and begged their lives. This attitude is entirely different from their arrogant behaviour at all times.

6. Japanese women were unwilling to let their husbands leave them, so they occupied the railway track and prevented the moving of trains. The cruel militarists however disregarded this and ordered the train to proceed. The train ran over and killed the women on the track. Several hundreds of women were killed in this way.

7. Wong Yuin Kao, a native of Shantung, who resides in San Yang Road, Chapei, was arrested by the Japanese who compelled him to set fire to houses. He refused, so the Japanese took out both of his eye-balls. Wong fell unconscious and was later rescued by the Red Cross Society.
pages.zh:
《战事画报》第 2 期。

1. 我军某军官在江湾作战时，遭刺刀攻击，致使肠子流出。然而他并未停歇，将肠子塞回体内后，继续与四五名敌军士兵搏斗。后被救援人员强行送往医院。途中他不断高呼：“杀！杀！”他确是一名勇敢的士兵。

2. 虽然敌军技艺不如我军，但其制服及其他装备远优于我军。当敌军被我军击毙后，其钢盔被我军缴获并佩戴。佩戴钢盔象征着我军已击杀敌军士兵，故是一种荣誉。目前前线大多数我军士兵均佩戴此类钢盔。

3. 当日军骑兵在江湾冲击我军防线时，我军向其投掷炭篓。这些炭篓阻碍了敌军前进，并造成敌军混乱。我军趁此机会发起冲锋，取得重大胜利。

4. 自战斗开始以来，数千名日军士兵阵亡，留其妻室在日本。后者已组织团体，要求政府让其丈夫回国。上海也出现了类似的运动。

5. 日军士兵被我军解除武装时，鞠躬乞求饶命。此种态度与其平日之傲慢行为截然不同。

6. 日本妇女不愿让丈夫离开，因而占据铁路轨道，阻止火车通行。然而残酷的军国主义者对此置之不理，命令火车继续行驶。火车碾过轨道，轧死妇女。数百名妇女以此方式丧生。

7. 王元高（Wong Yuin Kao，音译），山东人，居住于闸北三阳路，被日军逮捕并强迫其纵火烧屋。他拒绝服从，日军遂挖去其双眼。王昏迷不醒，后被红十字会救起。

pages.en:
BLOODY WAR. No.1

1. During the bombardment of the Woosung Forts,
the shells fired by enemy troops all fell on
the empty ground. They have no aim.

2. Japanese aeroplanes dropped bombs everywhere
setting people's houses on fire. There is no
humanity.

3. The Japanese military headquarters was hit by our
shells and many Japanese soldiers were killed.

4. Male and female workers of our Rescue Party
risked their lives by visiting the battle fields.
Their deeds are commendable.

5. The "Big Sword" Group fought continuously for 20
hours at Kiangwan. Their fame is wide spread.

6. When both sides meet face to face, our brave soldiers
defeated the enemy troops. The latter escaped
quickly.

No legal offence is disclosed. Much worse
statements have been made in reliable
Chinese Newspapers. But see Procla-
mation by S.M.C. entitled Emergency
measures Par. 2. sec. c. Why not con-
fiscate and destroy such papers without
preferring a charge? Persons violating
the curfew are detained over night
and destroying inflammatory literature
is no worse. (The Council) legally
speaking has no authority to issue
and enforce such proclamations but
times are not normal at present
and many technically illegal things
have to be done on the ground of
expediency.

R. Y. B.
M. Q.
Mar. 10, 1932.
pages.zh:
《血战》第 1 期

1. 在轰炸吴淞炮台期间，敌军发射之炮弹全部落在空地上。他们毫无准头。

2. 日本飞机四处投弹，点燃民宅。毫无人性可言。

3. 日军司令部被我军炮弹击中，多名日军士兵丧生。

4. 我方救援队之男女工作人员冒着生命危险奔赴战场。其事迹值得嘉许。

5. “大刀队”在江湾连续奋战 20 小时。其声名远播。

6. 当双方正面相遇时，我军英勇士兵击败敌军。后者迅速逃窜。

未发现法定犯罪行为。可靠的中文报纸上曾刊登更为恶劣之言论。但请参阅工部局题为《紧急措施》之公告第 2 条 c 款。为何不没收并销毁此类报刊而不提起公诉？违反宵禁者被拘留过夜，而销毁煽动性宣传品之举并不比此更甚。（董事会）在法律上无权发布和执行此类公告，但目前时局非正常，出于权宜之计，许多技术上非法之事不得不做。

R. Y. B.
M. Q.
1932 年 3 月 10 日。
